summary: Panel of independent analyses of HighwayHash beyond differential search, adversarially verified, then synthesized for the paper

synthesis.one_paragraph_answer: Add HighwayHash-64 to tab:injective:adversarial as a heuristic row with key 4 and bits 59.9* (GB/s cells from a clean rerun of the speed pass, not the loaded-machine scratchpad passes and not the design paper's AVX2 figures), and give it an appendix paragraph built on the one result that has a number, an explicit key and a reproducible command: a fixed 96-byte pair that collides in the full 1024-bit state, hence in HighwayHash-64/-128/-256 alike and under any suffix, with probability at least 2^-32 x 2^-24.3 = 2^-56.3 over a uniformly random key (exact 2^-32 weak-key condition hi32(k0)=hi32(init0[0]) that kills the first lane-0 multiply because the multipliers start public, times a measured 2^-24.3 second condition; 614 full-state collisions in 1.26e10 class keys across four independent runs; explicit key dbe6d5d5... hashing both messages to f5eba26391be727f, re-verified here against the byte-identical vendored reference). That is 2^7.7 above the ideal for the 64-bit output and caps the 128/256-bit outputs at 60 bits; it is also the designers' own two-packet cancellation strategy priced cheaper than their 2^-64 estimate. Around it the paper can state, with confirmed structural facts, why differential search finds nothing: absorption never mixes the lane pairs {0,1},{2,3}, the output reads lane 0, and only the four finalization rounds carry the keying; a reduced-round ladder (R=1: a -1 in the last word collides for 99.6% of keys; R=2: 2^-19.7; R=3: 0 collisions in 2^30 but a +2^40 difference leaves the top output bit biased by 2^-3.7; R=4: nothing in 2^31 keys, per-bit bias < 2^-13.9) shows the shipped fourth round is the first clean one, and word complements, the search's family, are blind after two rounds. Frame it with the literature facts (designers claim no proof, rounds chosen by an avalanche test, no third-party cryptanalysis found). Independently of HighwayHash, fix the pre-existing misstatement that SipHash and the Mersenne polynomial hash showed no collision in 2^30 SMHasher3 seeds (they ran 2^16/2^20 only; HighwayHash likewise 2^20 with a correlated seed). Do not claim HighwayHash matches SipHash-1-3, do not cite toy-model numbers, and do not present the 59.9 as more than the worst pair we found in one family.

ranked_recommendations.title: Structured weak-key pair: eps >= 2^-56.3 for a fixed 96-byte pair, full-state collision, table entry 59.9*
ranked_recommendations.why: The only finding that gives the table a number with an explicit key and a one-command check (./verify_standalone against the unmodified vendored reference, re-run in synthesis/). It is a full 1024-bit state collision, so it holds for HighwayHash-128/-256 and any suffix (2^72 / 2^200 above their ideals) and cannot be seen by unconditioned sampling (0 in 2^28). bits = log2(12 / 2^-56.3) = 59.9 at L=12 words. Pooled conditional rate 614/12,616,466,432 = 2^-24.29 (95%: 2^-24.41..2^-24.18); total is a lower bound on eps (only one weak-key class sampled, one family, one tuned constant), which is exactly the meaning of the table's asterisk. It is the designers' own two-packet cancellation strategy priced cheaper than their 2^-64 estimate because the dead first product leaves the second product's operands multiplication-free with a nearly constant top byte.
ranked_recommendations.evidence_status: confirmed: weak-keys-init claim 1 (refuter confirmed, corrected to 'at least 2^-56.3', reproducer confirmed with 59/2^30), claim 2 (both confirmed; refuter 1723/2^35 = 2^-24.25, reproducer 211/2^32 = 2^-24.28), claim 3 exact densities (both confirmed; refuter adds length-<32B shift, reproducer adds message-dependent v1-side dead events); synthesis recompiled verify_standalone against sha256 fb316726... copy: COLLIDE x3

ranked_recommendations.title: Structural facts to state as prose: lane pairs never mix during absorption, output reads lane 0, multipliers start public, key enters only v0/v1
ranked_recommendations.why: Explains both the weak-key pair and why the author's complement search finds nothing. Proven by code reading and verified empirically: with no finalization any difference confined to packet lanes 2,3 collides for every key and key[2], key[3] do not reach the output; per-lane first-packet multiply is dead with probability exactly 2^-32 per lane (weak values listed). This is the 'other way to think about it' the author asked for and needs no trial counts.
ranked_recommendations.evidence_status: confirmed: reduced-rounds claim 2 (both verifiers, 'packet lanes 2,3' precision), lane-locality claim 1 (both), weak-keys-init claim 3 (both), remainder-path claim 5 (same fact, consistent with confirmed claims)

ranked_recommendations.title: Reduced-round ladder: R=1 collides 99.6% (-1 in last word), R=2 2^-19.7, R=3 no collision but 2^-3.7 top-bit bias (+2^40), R=4 nothing at 2^31 keys; the fourth round is the first clean one
ranked_recommendations.why: Gives the appendix a cryptanalytic margin statement that does not depend on search and that a reader can rerun. Five lenses converge on the same numbers with independent code. Also the methodological point: word complements (the search family) are clean after two rounds, so they are the wrong probe for this design; single-byte differences in the last two lanes are the sensitive ones. Use the corrected numbers: 1-2^-8 = 99.6% (not 99.8/99.4 for the +2^40 joint events, which are 98.8%), bit 62 of the XOR difference equals 1 (sign fixed), 0 collisions in 2^30 at R=3, per-bit bias at R=4 bounded by 2^-13.9 simultaneously over 64 bits (2^-14.5 was the detection threshold, not a bound).
ranked_recommendations.evidence_status: confirmed with corrections: difference-bias claims 1-3 (refuters refuted wording/joint-vs-marginal numbers, reproducers confirmed all magnitudes incl. base independence), lane-locality claim 1 (both confirmed), structured-differences claims 1-3 (refuters refuted scope: rate is for the lowest bit of the byte; byte 5 is the bias-persistent class; reproducers confirmed), verify-siphash-baseline full sweep: R=3 biased for last-word bits 40-47 (|z| 319 at 2^22), R=4 clean at 2^28

ranked_recommendations.title: Fix the pre-existing SMHasher3 misstatement (SipHash, poly-mersenne never ran the 2^30 tier) and report HighwayHash's SMHasher3 result correctly
ranked_recommendations.why: appendix_adversarial.tex 175-179, experiments.tex 480-482 and MANIFEST.md 333-335 say SipHash and the Mersenne polynomial hash showed no collision in 2^30 seeds; the fork skips the extended tier for slow-registered hashes (SeedDifferentialTest.cpp:239/:262), so SipHash-2-4 ran 2^16, SipHash-1-3/poly-mersenne 2^20, HighwayHash-64 2^20 (FLAG_IMPL_SLOW, inherited upstream). The fork also keys HighwayHash as {1,2,3,4}^seed, a correlated family, so its PASS is not evidence under the paper's key model. Must be fixed regardless of the HighwayHash row.
ranked_recommendations.evidence_status: confirmed: paper-framing claims 1 and 2, both verifiers each (read-only file checks; one --extra run confirming no extended block)

ranked_recommendations.title: Literature framing: designers claim no proof, rounds chosen by a 3-byte avalanche test, no third-party cryptanalysis found
ranked_recommendations.why: Lets the paper say with primary-source quotes that HighwayHash's security evidence is the designers' statistical testing plus a hand argument they call 64-bit-only, that 6/10 rounds for 128/256 bits were added at the 2018 freeze with only a cost remark, and that no independent cryptanalysis was found (ePrint: no results; citing works are applications). Use the corrected wording: the 2023 issue-118 quote means they could not show a stronger bound, not that 2^-64 is unsupported; the designers did run smhasher low-weight differential tests; 'no third-party cryptanalysis found in these indexes' rather than 'none exists'.
ranked_recommendations.evidence_status: confirmed with wording corrections: literature claims 1-3 (each refuter refuted overreach in wording, each reproducer confirmed the sources verbatim; corrected claims supplied)

ranked_recommendations.title: Tail path has no key-free collision: length code (s<<32)+s separates residual lengths for every key; padding is not injective across lengths
ranked_recommendations.why: One or two sentences that pre-empt the obvious MUM-style question. Distinctness of the 1024-bit state for residual lengths 1..32 is a theorem (bijective block update after the code is added); empty-vs-one-block pins the key uniquely and that key is not a fixed point for the blocks tested; 3,522 structured pairs gave 0 collisions in 2^20 keys. Correction: the code is the only key-independent separator (the v1 rotation also separates all but a 2^{8(gcd-32)} fraction of keys).
ranked_recommendations.evidence_status: confirmed: remainder-path claim 1 (refuter narrowly refuted 'sole separator', reproducer confirmed with the same precision), claims 2 and 3 (both verifiers confirmed)

ranked_recommendations.title: Key-uniformity: key -> output map passes bias/chi-square/birthday/avalanche at R=4; avalanche fails at R=3 for <=32-byte messages (w3.b8 -> out63, p=0.009), at R=2 for 64-byte messages
ranked_recommendations.why: Optional single sentence: supports describing the finalization as PRF-like with a thin margin and records that full-key marginal statistics are uninformative (they pass even at R=1). Lower reader value than items 1-3 and it bounds nothing about message pairs; include only if space allows.
ranked_recommendations.evidence_status: confirmed with scope correction: key-uniformity claim 1 (both confirmed; targeted 2^26 check null), claim 2 (refuter refuted 'one round' as universal: 64-B margin is two rounds; reproducer confirmed numbers), claim 3 (both confirmed)

ranked_recommendations.title: Throughput cells: rerun the speed pass on an idle machine; do not import the design paper's 0.24 c/b or 5.2x SipHash
ranked_recommendations.why: No HighwayHash row exists in the committed speed files; three passes plus controls exist in the session scratchpad (speed_hh_pass{1,2,3}.jsonl, medians 4.5/6.2/6.3 GB/s at 16 KB and 5.0/6.0/7.5 at 512 B) but were taken under load (XXH3 control 12% under its committed value), so they support no throughput statement. The design paper's figures are Haswell/AVX2, 1 KiB, x86-only.

ranked_recommendations.title: Do not write that HighwayHash's margin equals SipHash-1-3's
ranked_recommendations.why: The 'same threshold of four rounds after injection' holds for one bit position and one distinguisher under a convention equating a SipRound with an Update; a full single-bit sweep shows HighwayHash R=3 biased for last-word bits 40-47 while R=4 is clean, i.e. zero spare rounds on that test, whereas SipHash's threshold survives the sweep. At most say that the complement differentials are uninformative on both designs (clean even for SipHash-1-0).
ranked_recommendations.evidence_status: siphash-baseline claim 1 confirmed (convention-dependent), claim 2 refuted by the refuter's full-position sweep (reproducer confirmed only the single-bit cells), claim 3 refuted as uninformative at 2^26 resolution

synthesis.table_row_proposal:
Insert after the komihash row in the 'heuristic, key <= 8 words' block of tab:injective:adversarial:

\texttt{HighwayHash}-64~\cite{highwayhash}     & 4 & 59.9$^*$ & [16KB] & [512B] \\

bits = log2(12 / 2^-56.3) = 59.9 at L = 12 words (96-byte pair; eps = 2^-32 exact x 2^-24.3 measured, pooled 614 collisions in 12,616,466,432 class keys over four independent runs; at all other lengths searched, 0/2^32, so the min over L is set by this pair). The asterisk carries its usual meaning (worst pair found; may be lower), and the prose should say that for HighwayHash only one family of pairs was explored. GB/s cells: fill from a clean rerun of ./speed with filter 'Highway' (3 passes + XXH3/komihash controls, speed_assemble.py); the scratchpad passes (medians 4.5/6.2/6.3 at 16 KB, 5.0/6.0/7.5 at 512 B) were taken under load and must not be used as-is. Optional: a caption clause 'the HighwayHash entry is a structured weak-key pair (\Cref{app:adversarial}); its 128- and 256-bit variants score the same' — or leave that to the prose. If the author prefers the paper-framing lens's separate sub-block 'keyed PRF designs, unproven, key <= 8 words', put the same row there; a SipHash-2-4 row is not recommended (not in hashes.h, no search, no speed pass).

% ===================================================================
% FILE 1: sections/injective.tex — table row (insert after the komihash row,
% inside the "heuristic, key <= 8 words" block).  [16KB]/[512B] are the two
% GB/s cells: fill from a clean speed pass, not from the loaded-machine passes

% ===================================================================
\texttt{HighwayHash}-64~\cite{highwayhash}     & 4 & 59.9$^*$ & [16KB] & [512B] \\

% ===================================================================
% FILE 1: sections/injective.tex — replace the paragraph beginning
% "\Cref{tab:injective:adversarial} gives the result." (lines ~285-294)
% ===================================================================
\Cref{tab:injective:adversarial} gives the result.  Within the budget the
proven methods score $57$--$64$ bits.  Of the heuristic methods, the four
built on a multiply--fold lose to a single differential: \texttt{wyhash},
\texttt{rapidhash} and \texttt{XXH3} to the all-ones difference on the two
words feeding their first fold, which collides with probability about
$2^{-27}$ under a random secret, some $2^{37}$ times the ideal; the $128$-bit
\texttt{XXH3-128} fares no better, because one of its two accumulators sees
only a raw word sum that the attacker can hold fixed; and \texttt{MUM} has
\emph{key-free} collisions, a fixed pair of $8$-byte messages that collides
for every seed.  \texttt{komihash} resisted every differential we tried at
$2^{32}$ seeds per surface, which bounds its score below only by our search
effort.  \texttt{HighwayHash}~\cite{highwayhash} resisted the same search, but
a structured $96$-byte pair that exploits its public initial multipliers
collides in its full $1024$-bit state with probability $2^{-56.3}$ over a
random $256$-bit key, $2^{7.7}$ above the ideal for its $64$-bit output; the
same pair therefore caps its $128$- and $256$-bit outputs at the same $60$
bits.  That entry, like the others marked~$^*$, is the worst pair we found,
and for \texttt{HighwayHash} only one family of such pairs was explored, so
the true score may be lower.  The attacks and their measurements are in
\Cref{app:adversarial}, which also records that the low $64$ bits of an
$89$-bit Mersenne residue are \emph{not} a safe output: a pair differing by
$2^{64}-1$ in the last word collides with probability $2^{-25}$, so the
Mersenne rows output the full residue.

% ===================================================================
% FILE 2: sections/appendix_adversarial.tex — new paragraphs, insert after
% the komihash paragraph and before "\paragraph{\texttt{MUM} v3.}"
% ===================================================================
\paragraph{\texttt{HighwayHash} (random key).}
\texttt{HighwayHash}-64~\cite{highwayhash}, the reference portable C
implementation (checked against its $66$ published test vectors), with the
four $64$-bit key words drawn uniformly at random per trial.  The state is
$1024$ bits in four lanes: two vectors $v_0,v_1$, into which the key is XORed
at reset, and two multiplier accumulators $\mathit{mul}_0,\mathit{mul}_1$ that
start as \emph{public} constants.  Each $32$-byte packet is added into $v_1$
lane-wise, each lane feeds one $32\times32\to64$-bit product into each
accumulator, and a fixed byte permutation (\emph{ZipperMerge}) mixes lanes
$0\leftrightarrow1$ and $2\leftrightarrow3$; the two lane pairs never
interact during absorption.  Four further rounds, each preceded by a lane
permutation that swaps the pairs, finalize, and the $64$-bit output is the
sum of the four lane-$0$ words.  Every step is a permutation of the state for
a fixed packet, so a collision is either a collision of the $1024$-bit state
or a coincidence of the $64$-bit truncation on two distinct states.

The differential search of the \texttt{komihash} paragraph found nothing:
single- and double-word complements and additive differences at every
position of a $32$-byte message ($15$ surfaces), and the complemented leading
pair at $32$--$160$ bytes, gave $0$ collisions in $2^{32}$ random keys each,
and two uniformly random messages $0$ in $2^{30}$ [confirm the remainder-path
cells of \texttt{run\_highway.sh} once they finish].  A structured pair does
better.  In lane $i$ of the first packet the product feeding
$\mathit{mul}_0$ is $\mathrm{lo}_{32}(v_1[i])\cdot\mathrm{hi}_{32}(v_0[i])$
with $v_0[i]=\mathrm{init}_0[i]\oplus k_i$, so when
$\mathrm{hi}_{32}(k_0)=\mathrm{hi}_{32}(\mathrm{init}_0[0])$, an event of
probability exactly $2^{-32}$, that product is zero and the lane-$0$
accumulators are untouched by the first packet.  For such keys the operands
of the lane-$0$ product of the second packet are functions of $k_0,k_1$ built
from additions, XORs and byte shuffles only, and their difference has a
nearly constant top byte.  A $96$-byte pair with differences $+2^{8}$,
$-(2^{9}+2^{24})$ and $+2^{8}$ in lane $0$ of its three packets, and the
second packet's constant chosen to match that top byte, then cancels the
state difference completely whenever one further $32$-bit relation holds,
which costs $2^{-24.3}$ rather than $2^{-32}$ ($614$ collisions in
$1.26\cdot10^{10}$ keys drawn from the $2^{-32}$ class, in four independent
runs; every collision is a full state collision).  The pair therefore collides
with probability at least $2^{-32}\cdot2^{-24.3}=2^{-56.3}$ over a uniformly
random key ($\pm0.15$ in the exponent), in HighwayHash-$64$, $-128$ and $-256$
alike and under any common suffix; an explicit key is
\texttt{dbe6d5d58afad71e a0142b42de197939 5bd2b2861106bd66 b6c304527caad524},
for which both messages hash to \texttt{f5eba26391be727f}.  With $L=12$
words this gives the $59.9$ bits of \Cref{tab:injective:adversarial},
$2^{7.7}$ above the ideal for the $64$-bit output and $2^{72}$ and $2^{200}$
above it for the wider ones.  The rate is far below what unconditioned
sampling can see ($0$ in $2^{28}$ random keys, as expected), and the pair is
the designers' own two-packet cancellation strategy, which their analysis
prices at $2^{-64}$ by charging $2^{-32}$ per product; the second charge is
cheaper because the first, dead product leaves the next operands
multiplication-free.  We tuned one constant of one family (lane $0$, byte
$1$); lane $2$ has the same geometry and other byte positions were not tried,
so a better pair of this kind may exist.

\paragraph{\texttt{HighwayHash} with fewer finalization rounds.}
Reducing the four rounds shows what they carry (the reduced copy reproduces
the published vectors at four).  With no finalization the output reads one
lane pair only: a difference confined to the last two lanes of a packet
collides for every key, and the output ignores $k_2$ and $k_3$ entirely.  With
one round a difference of $-1$ in the last word of a $32$-byte message
collides for $99.6\%$ of keys ($1-2^{-8}$); with two rounds it still collides
with probability $2^{-19.7}$ ($1610$ collisions in $2^{30.3}$ keys); with
three rounds no collision remained in $2^{30}$ keys, but a difference of
$+2^{40}$ in the same word leaves the top output bit biased by $2^{-3.7}$
($\Pr[\text{bit differs}]=0.422$ in two independent samples of $2^{30}$
keys); with the shipped four rounds no collision remained in $2^{31}$ keys and
no output bit was biased by more than $2^{-13.9}$ ($95\%$ bound over all $64$
bits).  The fourth round is thus the first at which this test sees nothing.
Word complements, the family our search uses, leave no trace after two
rounds; the sensitive differences are single bytes of the last two lanes,
which the byte permutation delivers to the output lane only through the
finalization.  The tail path adds no key-free collision: the padded packet is
not injective across lengths (a $4$-byte tail and the same tail followed by a
zero byte pad to the same block), but a length code $(s\ll32)+s$ added to
$v_0$ before the bijective block update separates residual lengths $1$--$32$
for every key, and none of $3{,}522$ structured length and padding pairs
collided in $2^{20}$ keys.

\paragraph{What is known about \texttt{HighwayHash}.}
Its designers write that they ``do not see a way to reduce the HighwayHash
algorithm to provably secure constructions'' and ``rely on statistical
testing''; their differential analysis is a hand argument that ``only
applies to the 64-bit case'', and the four finalization rounds were chosen by
an avalanche experiment over all $2^{24}$ three-byte inputs ($6$ and $10$
rounds for the $128$- and $256$-bit outputs were added when the design was
frozen in 2018 with a cost remark as the only rationale).  We found no
third-party cryptanalysis: the IACR ePrint archive has no entry mentioning
it, and its citing works are applications.  The entry in
\Cref{tab:injective:adversarial} is therefore an empirical bound from one
structured pair and a search, not a security level.

% FILE 2: sections/appendix_adversarial.tex — replace the last sentence of

% ===================================================================
In the extended tier \texttt{wyhash}, \texttt{rapidhash}, \texttt{XXH3} and
\texttt{XXH3-128} fail at about $2^{-26}$ on the complemented leading pair
and every \texttt{MUM} variant fails on the adjacent pairs at rate $1$, while
\texttt{komihash}, Polymur, \texttt{t1ha2}, FarmHash, CityHash and ChainHash
show no collision in $2^{30}$ seeds.  Implementations the suite registers as
slow receive only the default tier at $2^{20}$ seeds ($2^{16}$ for
SipHash-2-4) and no extended tier; SipHash, \texttt{HighwayHash} and the
Mersenne polynomial hash pass at that reduced resolution, which cannot see
rates below about $2^{-20}$.  (The suite also keys \texttt{HighwayHash} from
a single $64$-bit seed XORed into four fixed words, not from four independent
key words, so its verdict is not evidence under the key model of this
appendix.)

as slow and run only the default tier ($2^{16}$ and $2^{20}$ seeds), which

difference-bias 'deterministic at U=2' and 'exactly one Update of margin' for all differentials: holds for w3+2^40 only; w3-1 has one to two Updates. Draft states the two differentials separately.
reduced-rounds 'bit 62 of H1^H2 equals 0 for 99.1%': sign error (it equals 1); not used in the draft.

lane-locality claim 2 'every lane fully diffused at R=3, one spare round': refuted as an artifact of the lane-0 sum criterion (v0[0] low byte unchanged for 55% of keys at R=3; mul0[0] top byte 2x random at R=4); use only the collision numbers and the 2^-3.7 bias.
lane-locality 'narrow (one-byte) differences' label: the differentials were full-word complements and single-bit flips.

structured-differences 'most round-persistent class is lane 3 byte 0': collision-persistent only; byte 5 is bias-persistent one round longer. Also its README's '64:0 placement gives 0 collisions at every R>=1' is contradicted by its own data (2^-18.7 at R=1).
remainder-path 'c_s is the sole separator': the rotation also separates all but a 2^{8(gcd-32)} fraction of keys; draft says the code separates lengths for every key without calling it sole.

literature 'every security statement traces back to the designers' and 'arXiv full-text search': third-party statistical results and opinions exist and the arXiv API searches metadata only; draft says 'no third-party cryptanalysis found' with the indexes named.

literature 'designers used no automated search' and 'changed on statistical grounds until 2018-01-03': they ran smhasher low-weight differential sweeps, and the 2018 freeze commit cites only cost (the statistical change was January 2017). Draft wording corrected accordingly.
literature claim 5 (SipHash cryptanalysis lineage): medium confidence, one abstract unretrievable, and no verifier verdict; the draft cites no SipHash cryptanalysis paper.
paper-framing claim 3 'no throughput measurement exists, cells cannot be filled today': scratchpad passes exist; but they are loaded-machine and unusable, so the outcome (rerun) is the same.

paper-framing claims 4 and 5 (search progress snapshot; one-chain recurrence not Delta-universal) received no verifier verdicts; the Delta-universality remark is elementary but should be checked by the author before any Wegman-Carter wording is added, and the draft avoids that wording.

key-uniformity claim 2 'the margin is one round' as a universal statement: refuted for 64-byte messages (two rounds) and the residual is shared by key words 1 and 3; the draft does not include a key-uniformity sentence (optional item 7).
weak-keys-init densities 'independent of the message': for messages of 1..31 bytes the weak values shift with the length (densities unchanged); the draft states the condition for full packets only.
Any HighwayHash speed number from the design paper (0.24 c/b, 5.2x SipHash): Haswell AVX2, 1 KiB, not transferable to the M2 columns.

missing_angles: Optimisation and union of the weak-key trail (weak-keys-init). The 2^-56.3 figure samples ONE weak-key class (hi32(key[0]) = hi32(init0[0])) with ONE hand-chosen geometry (lane 0, byte 1, c1 = 0, c2lo tuned). Lane 2 has the same ZipperMerge geometry, the mul1 dead-key conditions (lo32(key[i]) = 4 further constants) and the message-dependent v1-side dead conditions (verifier: total dead-multiply density ~2^-28, not 2^-29/2^-30) give up to ~8-16 disjoint classes, and c1 / other byte positions were never scanned. Epsilon for the paper's table is the SUM over classes and the MAX over geometries; the current number is a lower bound on epsilon that could plausibly move by 2^3-2^5. Experiment: rerun ./wk cond with the other seven dead conditions and lane 2, scan c1 over 2^8-2^16 values at 2^26 keys each, and report the pooled epsilon.

Truncation collision after a MINIMAL state difference through the 4 finalization rounds. The weak-key trail leaves, after two packets, a state differing only by v1[0] -= 2^8 (verified). Nobody measured Pr[64-bit output collides | state differs by one byte in v1[0]] over the four PermuteAndUpdate rounds (state-level sampling, no key condition needed: draw 2^32 random 1024-bit states, add 2^8 to v1[0], run Finalize64). If that probability is far above 2^-64 (the reduced-rounds and lane-locality data show small additive differences diffuse slowly, and lane-locality's refuter found mul0[0] byte 7 unchanged for 0.78% of keys at the real R=4), a 64-byte pair scores 2^-56.3 * P_trunc, i.e. the two-packet version of the attack, and 'bits' = min over L would drop below 59.9 at L = 8 words. This is cheap (one afternoon at 3 threads) and directly affects the table entry.

Automated trail search for the absorb phase. Every reduced-round and weak-key result was hand-derived from the byte-permutation structure; no SAT/MILP/byte-level automated search for the cheapest key-conditioned differential trails (including trails that create and later cancel a mul0/mul1 difference, which weak-keys-init explicitly excludes) was attempted. The designers' own paper only hand-argued two sub-cases. A careful cryptographer would ask whether 2^-56.3 is the best three-packet trail or merely the first one found.

Cross-length pairs under the weak-key class. remainder-path proved distinct lengths separate the state via c_s = (s<<32)+s in v0, but only at 2^20 uniform keys; whether a later packet can cancel a v0 difference of (s-s')<<32 + (s-s') in all four lanes when the multiplies that read hi32(v0) are dead (the 2^-32 classes) was not examined. Also the length-shifted weak values for 1..31-byte messages (verifier of weak-keys claim 3) were found but not exploited.

Full-state / 128- and 256-bit consequences stated for the paper's key model only. All 319+59+25 weak-class hits collided at 128 and 256 bits, so HighwayHash-128/256 are capped at ~2^-56 for a fixed pair, 2^72/2^200 above ideal. No angle checked whether the 128/256-bit finalizers (6/10 rounds, other output lanes, lazymod127 reduction for 256) admit cheaper TRUNCATION collisions than the 64-bit one, nor whether the R=4 state-level residuals (mul0[0] top byte, mul lanes' biased bit 63 from difference-bias claim 5) leak into the 128-bit output that reads more lanes.

Distinguisher / PRF view of the weak-key class. The designers claim a PRF. Nobody measured whether an attacker observing outputs (chosen messages, hidden key) can detect that hi32(key[i]) hits one of the 2^-32 dead values (e.g. lane-i mul0 unchanged through packet 1 makes the first-packet output a multiplication-free function of the key), or recover key bits from it. This is outside the paper's collision metric but is what 'PRF-like' wording in the suggested texts would imply; without it the paper should not describe the design as PRF-like.

Consistency of the finalization-round 'margin' narrative with the state-level attack. reduced-rounds, difference-bias, lane-locality, structured-differences, key-uniformity and siphash-baseline all frame HighwayHash's security as 'four finalization rounds, one (or zero, or two) spare'. The best attack found (weak-keys-init) is a full-state collision in the absorb phase that the finalization cannot repair at any round count. No angle reconciles these; the paper must say the round margin concerns truncation collisions only, and that the measured epsilon comes from the absorb phase.

Message-length dependence of the table metric. bits = min_L log2(L/epsilon) was evaluated at L = 12 words only (59.9). The paper's other rows use the worst L over 32-160 B; for HighwayHash the same pair with a common suffix (verified to survive suffixes) at L = 20 words gives 60.6, but shorter L may be worse (see the two-packet truncation angle). Nobody computed the min over L.

SMHasher3 evidence under the wrong key model. The fork seeds HighwayHash as key[i] = {1,2,3,4}[i] ^ seed64 (four correlated words), runs it at 2^20 seeds and never the extended tier (FLAG_IMPL_SLOW). The paper-framing lens caught the tier issue, but no angle states that the SeedDifferential PASS is not evidence under the table's four-independent-words model, nor that SipHash-2-4 (2^16) / SipHash-1-3 / poly-mersenne (2^20) are currently misreported as 2^30 in three .tex files and MANIFEST.md (this correction is needed regardless of HighwayHash).

Throughput fairness. The only HighwayHash speed data are three loaded-machine scratchpad passes (4.5-6.3 GB/s at 16 KB, XXH3 control 12% below its committed value); they use Google's reference HHStateNEON (speed_hashes.h:37, checked), but HighwayHash was designed for AVX2 and its NEON path is known to be slower. No idle-machine rerun, no x86/AVX2 companion number (the author has an x86 Xeon host), and no statement that the M2 column is the design's weaker platform. Also the author's memory rule 'make no timing claims on the shared machine' applies to all dossier numbers.

Verification of the vendored SIMD implementations against the portable C. Every experiment used the portable C; the table would time the NEON C++ class. Nobody checked that HHStateNEON reproduces kExpected64 (the selftest reports 66/66 for 'HighwayHash64', which is hashes.h's portable Highway64, not Highway64Neon). One 66-vector check on the NEON path closes this.

Base-message dependence of whole-byte and multi-bit differentials at R=4. All R=4 'nothing detected' cells used one or two base messages; the R<4 whole-byte XOR results were shown to be base-dependent (structured-differences refuter: byte4_L2 2^-2.6 at 32 B vs 2^-23.7 at 64 B). No angle swept base messages at R=4 for the strongest reduced-round classes (lane-3 bytes 0 and 5, w3+/-2^40) beyond 2-3 bases.

Pending background runs are cited as if finished. toy-model's Toy B / Toy C 2^32 sweeps (verifier: enum process no longer running, no 'done' after the first job), structured-differences' 39-class 2^26 grid and 2^28 precision file (verifier: precision_L3byte5 file did not exist), and the author's own run_highway.sh length/remainder cells were incomplete at report time. Nothing from them should enter the paper until the ALLDONE/CDONE/ALL_DONE markers and results_highway.md are checked.
unverified_claims: Claims with NO verifier verdict at all in the dossier (neither refuter nor reproducer): reduced-rounds claims 4 (w0+2^32 diffusion trail, 'R=4 one round beyond full state diffusion') and 5 (R=0 high-32 collision 2^-2.7); difference-bias claims 4 (wyhash bias-test calibration, 'bias tests blind below ~2^-12') and 5 (mul0/mul1 top-bit bias 0.11 at R=4, P = 1/2 - ln2/2; medium confidence); lane-locality claims 4 (bit-63 flip in lane 2 collides for half the keys at r=1) and 5 (nothing at R=4 in 2^26); weak-keys-init claim 4 ('no packet-1 pair can equalise v0; a full-state collision needs at least three packets' -- explicitly heuristic for later packets); remainder-path claims 4 (3,522 structured pairs, 0 collisions at 2^20) and 5 (R=0 last-byte-flip key-free collision at 56 lengths); toy-model claim 4 (qualitative, low confidence, depends on unfinished sweeps); literature claims 4 (SMHasher/rurban pass, issue #5 2^-62 variant) and 5 (four SipHash third-party papers; CANS 2019 abstract never retrieved, medium confidence; Dobraunig DOI from a search page, SipHash INDOCRYPT bib data from memory); paper-framing claims 4 (search status; time-dependent) and 5 (one-chain recurrence not Delta-universal; elementary but nobody checked whether the paper claims AXU anywhere); structured-differences claims 4 and 5; siphash-baseline claims 4 and 5; key-uniformity claims 4 and 5 (claim 5 'key word 3 -> bit 63 diffuses last' is contradicted in part by the claim-2 refuter, who found key word 1 bits 8-13 carry the identical residual).

structured-differences claim 4 ('any difference placed in a packet followed by one more packet gives 0 collisions at every R>=1') is contradicted by the claimant's own sweep_bits_64B_p0 file and by two reproducers' side notes (lane-3 bit 0 in the first packet collides at R=1 with rate 2^-18.7; lane-3 bit 40 gives 3-4 hits in 2^20 at R=1). It was never formally verified and is false as stated.

Refuter/reproducer disagreement resolved only by re-scoping: siphash-baseline claim 2 ('HighwayHash-64 has one spare round, same as SipHash-1-3'). The reproducer confirmed it for bit 63 of the last word; the refuter's full 256-position sweep shows R=3 is strongly biased for last-word bits 40-47 (|z| up to 319 at 2^22, output bit 63), so by the same criterion the shipped hash has ZERO spare rounds for those positions, while SipHash's threshold of 4 survives all positions. structured-differences (both verifiers) independently confirm the R=3 lane-3 byte-5 bias. Treat 'one spare, same as SipHash-1-3' as refuted.

Refuter/reproducer disagreement on interpretation, data agree: reduced-rounds claim 1 ('collision floor reached at R=1, three rounds below R=4') -- 0/2^27 bounds each cell at 2^-25.4 only and cannot distinguish R=1 from R=4; the reproducer confirmed the counts, the refuter the overreach. The same pattern applies to difference-bias claim 1 (bound 2^-14.5 is the detection threshold, not a bound; 26 not 54 distinct pairs) and siphash-baseline claim 3 (the harness-style differentials at 2^26 keys cannot see the paper's 2^-27-scale effects, so 'do not discriminate round counts' is a statement about the test's resolution).

Numbers in claims that both verifiers agree are wrong and must not be copied into the paper: difference-bias claim 2's '99.8%' (H(m') = H(m)+2^48 at R=1) and '99.4%' (zero low byte at R=2) are both 98.8% = (255/256)^3; reduced-rounds claim 3's 'bit 62 of H1^H2 equals 0 for 99.1%' has the polarity flipped (equals 1); difference-bias claim 3 misattributes the '0.98-0.99 zero top byte at U=3' (belongs to w3-1, not w3+2^40, whose U=3 top-byte-zero rate is 0.65) and omits that w3+2^40 at 64 B has the largest reduced-round collision rate (2^-18.5 at U=3); toy-model claim 2's R=1 ratios (1.35x/1.85x) come from a non-uniform 2^24 key prefix and flip direction over the full 2^32 space (0.81x/2.85x); literature claim 3 attaches 'on statistical grounds' to the 2018-01-03 round-count change whose only stated rationale is cost; literature claim 2's reading of the 2023 maintainer quote is inverted (he could not demonstrate a LOWER attack probability than 2^-64, not that the 2^-64 figure was undemonstrated).

weak-keys-init claim 1's headline is a lower bound, not an estimate: 'collides with probability 2^-56.3' should read 'at least about 2^-56.3 (95% CI 2^-56.5..2^-56.2 from 344 hits in 7.25e9 class keys)'; contributions from the other weak-key classes and geometries were not measured. Both verifiers confirmed the number and the explicit colliding key; the top-byte confinement {4c..4f} of D0 is empirical (2^31 + 2^30 + 5x2^32 exhaustive-in-L samples), not proven.

lane-locality claim 2 and all 'fully diffused at R=3 / one spare round' statements: the refuter showed the 64-bit-sum avalanche criterion is blind to the state; at the real R=4, mul0[0] byte 7 is unchanged for 0.78% of keys (2x random, ~127 sigma) and mul1[0] byte 0 for 0.59% after a -1 difference in lane 3, and even a wide complement leaves 0.43-0.45% (>=13 sigma). This R=4 state-level non-randomness was found only by a verifier, has no reproducer, and its output-level consequences (e.g. for the 128-bit finalizer or for additive output differences) were not examined.

paper-framing claim 3 ('no throughput measurement exists, GB/s cells cannot be filled today'): refuter found three scratchpad passes from 12:16 on a loaded machine; reproducer confirmed none exist in the tree. Both are right about their scope; the usable status is 'noisy preliminary numbers exist, nothing publishable'.

The literature negative ('no third-party cryptanalysis') is a universal negative from index searches: dblp bot-blocked for everyone, arXiv API is metadata-only (CedrusDB counter-example), full texts of two 2025-2026 theses and one SIGCOMM paper unread. Safe only as 'we found none in ePrint, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, Crossref and Google Scholar'.
risks: Internal contradiction between angles if adopted verbatim. paper-framing's table option and appendix paragraph list HighwayHash as '>=32*' with 'resisted every differential we tried'; weak-keys-init supplies a verified fixed pair with epsilon >= 2^-56.3, i.e. bits <= 59.9 at L = 12 words. The published entry must be the found pair (an upper bound on bits, starred because a better pair may exist), not a search-effort lower bound; and the injective.tex sentence 'komihash and HighwayHash resisted every differential' becomes false.

Overclaiming a 'weak-key attack' or 'break'. In the paper's own metric HighwayHash-64 scores ~60 bits, inside the 57-64 band of the proven hashes and 2^7.7 above ideal; wyhash/rapidhash/XXH3 are 2^37 above ideal and MUM is key-free. Wording like 'weak keys', 'structured state collisions' or 'caps the 128/256-bit outputs at 60 bits' is accurate but must sit next to the statement that for the 64-bit output this is the best result among the heuristic hashes and not a practical attack (2^56 keys).

Misrepresenting the designers. The suggested texts quote the 2023 maintainer comment as calling the 2^-64 figure 'not necessarily tight' in the weak direction; the full quote says the true probability 'might actually be lower'. The paper can correctly say the weak-key pair shows the 2^-64 hand estimate is not an upper bound (its sub-case assumed independent 2^-32 events and uniform v0, v1; the attack pays 2^-24.3 for the second condition because the operands are correlated), but must quote the paper's 'at most 1 in 2^64' as a per-strategy estimate under stated assumptions, and note the README's 'formal security analysis' vs the paper's 'absence of a formal proof' tension without ridicule.

Attributing security to the finalization rounds. Six angles produce 'four rounds, one/zero/two spare' statements at 2^20-2^30 resolution; none of these bear on the measured epsilon, which arises in the absorb phase and survives any number of finalization rounds. A reader would infer that adding a fifth round fixes the finding; it does not. Conversely the 'one spare round' figure is position-dependent (zero for lane-3 byte 5 by the bias criterion, two for 64-byte messages by the key-avalanche criterion) and must not be quoted as a single number, nor compared to SipHash-1-3 (whose threshold survives all positions).

Unfair speed comparison. HighwayHash's GB/s cells would come from loaded-machine NEON passes on a design tuned for AVX2; 'several times slower' on M2 could be reported without noting the platform. Any HighwayHash speed number needs an idle rerun with controls, a NEON-vs-reference-vector check of HHStateNEON, and a footnote that the AVX2 path (0.24 c/B on Haswell per the design paper) is the design target.

Presenting 2^-N 'clean' results as evidence of strength. All R=4 null results bound per-bit bias at ~2^-12..2^-14.5 and collision rates at ~2^-24..2^-29; the paper's other heuristic rows are separated at 2^-27 with 2^32 keys. Sentences of the form 'no bias detected after the fourth round' should carry the resolution explicitly, and 'indistinguishable from a random function' (key-uniformity) should not appear without 'at the tested sample sizes'.

Reduced-round numbers with known errors leaking into text: 99.8%/99.4% (should be 98.8%), 'bit 62 = 0' (should be 1), '19 biased bits' (sample-size dependent), 'deterministic at U=2' (near-deterministic), the 2^24-prefix toy ratios, and 'lane-3 byte 0 is the most round-persistent class' (byte 5 persists a round longer by bias). All were flagged by at least one verifier; the suggested_text fields of reduced-rounds and difference-bias still contain some of them.

Under-stating epsilon. Because only one weak class and one geometry were sampled, the table's 59.9 could be optimistic for HighwayHash; the star convention ('may be lower') covers this, but the caption must say the star means 'a better pair may exist' for HighwayHash and 'no pair found' for komihash -- two different meanings of the same mark.

Claiming the finalization is a permutation/'every round is a permutation' or 'only truncation collisions' without checking the 128/256 finalizers: remainder-path and paper-framing derive this from the 64-bit code path; the 256-bit finalizer includes a modular reduction (lazymod127) that was not examined.

Citing the SMHasher3 results for HighwayHash at all: the fork's correlated-key seeding and the 2^20 default tier mean the PASS is neither under the paper's key model nor at the paper's sensitivity. The existing 2^30 claims for SipHash and poly-mersenne (three .tex files, MANIFEST.md) are already wrong and would be compounded by adding HighwayHash to that list.

Timing of the report. Several claims rest on background jobs that had not finished (toy-model sweeps, structured-differences 2^26/2^28 grid, the author's own run_highway.sh length/remainder cells). Text drafted now ('every surface gave 0 collisions in 2^32 keys') asserts coverage that has not been run.

res.summary: Built a copy of the HighwayHash C reference with a configurable number R of PermuteAndUpdate finalization rounds (R=4 reproduces all 66 published kExpected64 vectors; upstream test prints "Test success"; R=0..3 differ from R=4 on all 260 checks). For each key the base and every variant message are absorbed once and the states advanced one round at a time, so all R share the same key stream. Full 64-bit collision rates over 134,217,726 random 4-word keys per cell (3 threads, floor(2^27/3) each) at 32 B and 64 B: every cell is 0 hits at R=1,2,3,4 for all differentials (~w0~w1, ~w0, ~w3, w0+2^32, w0^lo32, unrelated random control, plus ~w7 and w4+2^32 at 64 B); the only non-zero cells are R=0 with a difference confined to lanes 2,3 (~w3 at both lengths, ~w7 at 64 B), which collide for ALL keys because ZipperMerge only pairs lanes 0<->1 and 2<->3 and the 64-bit output reads lane 0, so without a Permute lanes 2,3 never reach the output (also verified: at R=0 the output is independent of key[2], key[3] in 100,000/100,000 trials, and depends on all four key words at R=1). So the smallest R at which every full-width rate is at the sampling floor is R=1. Half-width collisions: at R=0 the high 32 bits collide with rate 2^-2.7 for w0+2^32 (32 B) and 2^-2.4 for w4+2^32 (64 B) because the output difference is confined to the low ~38 bits (bits 45..63 of the XOR difference are 0 for all keys); at R>=1 all 140 half-width cells show 0 or 1 hit out of 2^27 (5 single hits, 4.3 expected under the ideal 2^-32). Output-difference bit bias measured on every key at n=4,194,303 (4 sigma = 0.0010): at R=1 the ~w3 pair (32 B) has 19 bits beyond 4 sigma with max bias 0.4907 (bit 62 of H1^H2 is 0 for 99.1% of keys) and ~w7 (64 B) has 12 bits (max 0.4008); at R=2,3,4 no bit of any differential at either length exceeds 4 sigma, so the smallest R with an unbiased output difference is R=2. State-word diffusion over 16,777,215 keys shows a slow trail for the high-half additive difference w0+2^32: mul0[0] is unchanged for ALL keys at R=0 (the multiply reads only lo32(v1)), mul0[2]/mul0[3] unchanged for 99.997%/99.998% at R=1, mul0[1]/mul0[2] still unchanged for 33.2%/33.9% of keys at R=2, and all 16 words differ for every key only from R=3; w4+2^32 at 64 B shows the same trail (R=2: 37.7%/38.5% unchanged). The four lane-0 state words are never all equal at any R>=1 for any differential. Net margin picture for the published R=4: 3 rounds above the collision floor, 2 rounds above bit-uniformity of the output difference, 1 round above full state diffusion of the slowest trail found. No R=0 differential gave a key-independent NON-zero output difference: distinct differences over 2^16 keys were 65536 (or 65535) for every differential except the lane-2/3 ones, whose difference is identically 0.

experiments.name: vectors_check (modified copy reproduces upstream)
experiments.parameters: cc -O2 -I. c/highwayhash.c c/highwayhash_test.c; cc -O2 -I. c/highwayhash.c vectors_check.c; kTestKey1 lengths 0..64, kTestKey2 33 B; R=0..3 vs R=4
experiments.result: upstream test: 'Test success'; HighwayHash64R(.,.,.,4)==HighwayHash64==kExpected64 for all 65 lengths and the 33-byte key2 vector; R<4 outputs differ from R=4 in 260/260 cases

experiments.name: rates_27: full/half-width collisions vs R
experiments.parameters: ./rr rates 27 3 1 rates_27.csv 6 -> 3 threads x 44,739,242 = 134,217,726 keys per cell; seeds 1 (32 B) and 2 (64 B); key stream Rng(seed*0x9E3779B97F4A7C15+7919*t+1) as in the harness; base = base_msg(len,12345), control = base_msg(len,67890); differentials ~w0~w1, ~w0, ~w3, w0+2^32, w0^lo32, ctrl, and at 64 B also ~w7, w4+2^32; R=0..4; bias on every 64th key (n=2,097,153)
experiments.result: Full 64-bit: ~w3 R=0 134,217,726/134,217,726 (32 B and 64 B), ~w7 R=0 134,217,726/134,217,726 (64 B); every other cell, including all R>=1 cells, 0/134,217,726. High-32: w0+2^32 R=0 21,042,973/2^27 = 2^-2.7 (32 B); w4+2^32 R=0 26,089,772/2^27 = 2^-2.4 (64 B); lane-2/3 differentials all keys at R=0; all R>=1 half-width cells 0 or 1 hit (5 single hits across 140 cells; 4.3 expected at 2^-32). Bias (n=2^21, 4sigma=0.0014): R=1 ~w3 19 bits, max 0.4906; ~w7 11 bits, max 0.4007; R>=2 nothing beyond 4 sigma. Wall 2 min 29 s

experiments.name: bias_22: output-difference bit bias on every key
experiments.parameters: ./rr2 rates 22 3 5 bias_22.csv 0 -> 4,194,303 keys per cell, seeds 5/6, bias_shift 0; per-bit probabilities in bias_22.csv.bits.csv; bits_report.py threshold 0.05
experiments.result: R=2,3,4: max |bias| <= 0.0008, 0 bits beyond 4 sigma (0.0010) for all 14 (length,differential) cells. R=1: 32 B ~w3 19 bits beyond 4 sigma, max 0.4907 (bit62=0 w.p. 0.991, bit3=1 w.p. 0.900, bit5=1 w.p. 0.759); 64 B ~w7 12 bits, max 0.4008 (bit63=1 w.p. 0.901); 64 B ~w3 1 bit at 0.0029; 64 B w4+2^32 2 bits at 0.0010 (borderline). R=0: w0+2^32 33 bits (bits 45..63 always 0, 38..44 nearly 0); w4+2^32 31 bits; ~w3/~w7 all 64 bits constant 0; ctrl bit0=1 w.p. 0.778; w0^lo32 bit63=1 w.p. 0.634. Full collisions 0/4,194,303 at all R>=1. Wall 12 s

experiments.name: diffusion_24: Pr[state word differs] per (differential, R)
experiments.parameters: ./rr2 diffusion 24 3 11 diffusion_24.csv -> 16,777,215 keys, seeds 11 (32 B) / 12 (64 B); 16 state words + lane-0 all-equal count; R=0..4

experiments.name: examples_16: R=0 output difference structure
experiments.parameters: ./rr examples 16 4242 -> 65,536 keys, both lengths, all differentials; distinct XOR and additive output differences at R=0 and R=1; three concrete keys printed per differential
experiments.result: Distinct R=0 output differences over 65,536 keys: 65,536 for ~w0~w1, ~w0, w0^lo32, ctrl (XOR and additive); 65,536 XOR / 65,535 additive for w0+2^32 and w4+2^32 (additive differences small, e.g. 0xb211a453, 0x29f862df0, 0x227d2262b, i.e. confined to the low ~34-38 bits); exactly 1 (= 0) for ~w3 and ~w7. At R=1 all differentials give 65,536 distinct differences. No non-zero key-independent difference found

experiments.name: key_indep_check: which key words the output sees
experiments.parameters: cc -O2 -I. c/highwayhash.c key_indep_check.c; 100,000 random keys, 32/64 B alternating, re-randomise one key word at a time, R=0 and R=1
experiments.result: R=0: output changed 100,000/100,000 times for key[0] and key[1], 0/100,000 for key[2] and key[3]. R=1: 100,000/100,000 for all four

claims.claim: With R>=1 finalization rounds no tested fixed pair collides on the full 64-bit output in 134,217,726 random keys per cell, at 32 B and 64 B, for all eight differentials; the collision floor is reached at R=1, three rounds below the published R=4.
claims.evidence: rates_27.md: every full-64-bit cell with R in {1,2,3,4} reads 0 / 2^27 (exact count 134,217,726 in rates_27.csv); bias_22.md repeats 0/4,194,303 with different seeds.
claims.how_to_check: cd <dir>; cc -O3 -I. -c c/highwayhash.c -o hh.o; c++ -std=c++17 -O3 -I. rr.cpp hh.o -o rr2 -lpthread; ./rr2 rates 27 3 1 out.csv 6 | grep -A9 'Full 64-bit' ; every R>=1 cell must be '0 / 2^27'

claims.claim: With no finalization (R=0) any difference confined to message lanes 2,3 collides for every key: ZipperMerge pairs lanes 0<->1 and 2<->3 only, the 64-bit output reads lane 0, and without a Permute the output does not depend on key[2], key[3].

res.paper_relevance: Gives the paper a cryptanalytic, non-differential-search way to characterise HighwayHash's margin in the adversarial section or appendix: the 4 finalization rounds sit 3 rounds above the point where fixed-pair collisions vanish (R=1), 2 rounds above output-bit uniformity (R=2), and 1 round above full state diffusion of the slowest trail we found (R=3, a high-half additive difference that the 32x32 multiplies do not see until the Permute swaps halves). It also supplies a clean structural statement: without finalization HighwayHash-64 reads only lane 0, so a change in the last two lanes of a packet is a certain collision and only 128 of the 256 key bits matter; the finalization rounds, not the absorb, are what make the heuristic hash keyed on the whole message. This supports listing HighwayHash as a heuristic hash whose 'bits' entry is a search bound (no collision found at 2^27 keys for these pairs), while noting that its margin argument is empirical rather than a proof.
res.suggested_text: HighwayHash-64 finalizes with four PermuteAndUpdate rounds; reducing that number is the usual way to gauge a heuristic design's margin.  With the rounds removed entirely, the 64-bit output reads a single lane, so a difference confined to the last two lanes of a packet collides for every key and only two of the four key words affect the output.  One round removes every fixed-pair collision we tested (0 in 2^27 random keys per pair, at 32 and 64 bytes), two rounds remove all detectable bias in the output difference (no bit beyond four standard deviations at 2^22 keys), and three rounds are needed before a high-half additive difference, which the 32x32-bit multiplies do not see until the permutation swaps halves, has reached every state word.  The published four rounds thus leave one round of margin over full diffusion of the slowest trail we found; this is evidence of a comfortable design, not a bound on its collision probability.
res.caveats: Sampling floor is 2^-27 per cell (134,217,726 keys); 'at the floor' means 0 hits, not a bound near 2^-64. Only eight fixed differentials at two lengths (32 B one packet, 64 B two packets, no remainder path) were tested; the R at which a rate reaches the floor is specific to these pairs and other differentials may need more rounds. The 'full state diffusion at R=3' statement is at 2^24-key resolution (a word that differs for all 16,777,215 keys may still be equal with probability below ~2^-24). The 1/3 fraction of keys with mul0[1], mul0[2] unchanged at R=2 is measured, not derived. The R=0 certain collision and key[2]/key[3] independence follow from the code structure (no cross-pair mixing without Permute) and were verified empirically, but no formal proof was written. Bit-bias 'none beyond 4 sigma' is a per-bit marginal test only; joint or linear-combination biases were not tested. The rates_27 run was produced by the first build (binary rr) whose arithmetic is identical to rr2 but whose table header rounds the key count; exact counts are in the CSV. No timing or throughput claims; the machine was shared with load average 170-255 and runs used 3 threads.

(3) Line audit of rr.cpp found no bug: per-thread distinct RNG seeding, fresh state per message per key, key = four 64-bit words, message lengths 32/64 with no remainder path, base and variant buffers distinct, bias counted on every key when bias_shift=0. Their c/highwayhash.c diff vs the vendored original is purely additive (exposes ProcessAll/Output64/round count), HighwayHash64 still calls 4 rounds. (4) One transcription error in the claim text and their README: 'bit 62 of H1^H2 equals 0 for 99.1% of keys' — their own raw data (bias_22.csv.bits.csv row 32,~w3,1,62,4194303,4155444 => ones/n = 0.9907) and their bits_report output ('b62=1(0.991)') say bit 62 equals 1, and my run agrees (0.9908). Magnitude, bit index and count are right; only the polarity in the prose is wrong. Not re-run: the 2^27 rates table, the diffusion table, key-independence check. Reproduction commands are in README.md (also README_bias_claim.md, since the directory is shared with another reproducer) in the repro-reduced-rounds directory; each 2^22 run took ~14 s wall on 2 threads (no throughput claim).
v.corrected_claim: The output XOR difference is statistically uniform per bit (no bit beyond 4 sigma at n=4,194,303, 4 sigma = 0.0010) from R=2 on for every differential tested, but at R=1 the lane-2/3 differentials leave near-constant output bits (~w3 at 32 B: 19 bits, bit 62 of H1^H2 equals 1 for 99.1% of keys and bit 3 equals 1 for 90.0%; ~w7 at 64 B: 12 bits, bit 63 equals 1 for 90.1%). Independently reproduced with a separate implementation and key stream (2^22 keys, two seeds), and the same qualitative pattern (17 and 14 biased bits at R=1, none at R>=2) holds for a different base message.

res.summary: Measured bias in D_xor = H(m)^H(m') and D_sub = H(m)-H(m') of HighwayHash-64 over uniformly random 4-word keys, for attacker-fixed pairs, at 1, 2, 3 and 4 finalization rounds (R=4 = the real hash; the modified C copy reproduces all 66 published test vectors). Per-bit z-scores, byte chi-squares, Hamming-weight tests and exact-collision counts. (1) Real hash, R=4: NO statistic exceeded |z|=3.83 in any of 54 (pair,length,D) configurations at 2^28 keys, nor in two pooled 2^30 samples (2^31 total) of the strongest reduced-round pair; per-bit bias < 2^-14.5 and collision rate < 2^-29.4 (95%) for that pair. (2) Reduced rounds are very weak and the weakness is NOT in the word-complement family the paper's search uses: a small ADDITIVE difference is the right differential for this byte-shuffling design. w3 -= 1 (equivalently the zero message vs. zero with w3 = all-ones) collides for 99.6% of keys at R=1, 2^-19.7 at R=2 (1610/2^30.3), and at R=3 still leaves bit 63 of D_xor biased by 2^-13.4 (pooled z=6.87, two independent seeds). A 64-cell scan of wK +/- 2^(8j) found w3 +/- 2^40 much stronger: at R=1 the output difference is DETERMINISTIC (H(m') = H(m) + 2^48 for 99.8% of keys), at R=2 the low byte of D is 0 for 99.4% of keys, and at R=3 bit 63 of D_xor has bias 2^-3.7 (0.0782 in both 2^30 samples) with the high byte of D_sub far from uniform (chi-square p < 1e-300). (3) Counting Updates U after the injecting packet (real hash: U >= 5 for the last packet): signal is deterministic at U=2, collision 2^-19.7 or top-byte-zero w.p. 0.99 at U=3, bias 2^-1.06 (64 B, first packet, R=2) to 2^-3.7 (32 B, R=3) at U=4, and undetectable at U=5 (2^28-2^31 keys). The real hash therefore has exactly one Update of margin over the detectable regime at this sensitivity. (4) Word complements (c0..c3, c01), +2^32 and single-bit flips all vanish by R=2 (R=1 leaks for lanes 1-3, bias up to 2^-1). (5) State-level diffusion (2^25 keys): the raw multiply lanes mul0/mul1 keep a biased top bit even after 4 rounds (bit 63 of mul0[2]: bias ~0.11; product top bit has P=1/2-ln2/2=0.153 and the XOR accumulation decays only geometrically), but the output adds the unbiased v0/v1 lanes and shows no key-uniformity bias (H(m) itself max |z|=3.24 at 2^25). (6) Calibration: the same bias test on wyhash 4.3's (M,M) pair sees its 2^-27 collision structure only as 2 exact collisions in 2^28 and zero bias, confirming that bias tests and collision counting are complementary (per-bit bias at 2^28 detects collision structure only above ~2^-12).

res.paper_relevance: The paper's table scores hashes by collision probability found by differential search; HighwayHash is not yet in it. This angle gives two things the table cannot: (a) a security-margin statement for the heuristic design, phrased in rounds rather than in collision rate: with the strongest attacker-chosen pairs we found (an additive 2^40 or -1 difference on the last lane), the output difference of HighwayHash-64 is fully predictable after one finalization round, still 2^-3.7-biased after three, and indistinguishable from uniform (per-bit bias < 2^-14.5, 2^31 keys) after the fourth, i.e. the hash keeps exactly one Update of margin over the detectable regime; and (b) a methodological caveat for the appendix: bias tests at 2^28-2^31 keys are blind to the 2^-27 exact-cancellation flaws that define the wyhash/rapidhash/XXH3 rows (verified on wyhash itself), so the HighwayHash row's collision entry must come from counting, and the 0-in-2^31 result here only supports 'no collision above 2^-29.4 found for these pairs' (an entry of the form >= 29* by the table's convention, i.e. a search-effort lower bound like komihash). The reduced-round facts also tell the orchestrator's differential search which family to add: small additive differences (+-1, +-2^40 on w3; +-2^32/2^56 on w2) rather than complements.
res.suggested_text: HighwayHash (random 256-bit key). Its finalizer applies four rounds of the same Update to the state; we measured how much of the four is needed. For a fixed pair differing by $+2^{40}$ in the last $64$-bit word of a $32$-byte message, the one-round output satisfies $H(m')=H(m)+2^{48}$ for $99.8\%$ of random keys, after two rounds the low byte of $H(m)\oplus H(m')$ is zero for $99.4\%$ of keys, and after three rounds the top bit of $H(m)\oplus H(m')$ is still biased by $2^{-3.7}$; after the fourth round no per-bit bias above $2^{-14.5}$ and no collision remained in $2^{31}$ keys. A difference of $-1$ in the same word collides after one round for $99.6\%$ of keys and after two rounds with probability $2^{-19.7}$ ($1610$ collisions in $2^{30.3}$ keys). Word complements, the differential family used for the other heuristic hashes, leave no trace after two rounds. These bias measurements are complementary to collision counting: on \texttt{wyhash}'s $(M,M)$ pair the same statistics see no bias at $2^{28}$ secrets while the direct count records its $2^{-27}$ collisions, so the HighwayHash entry rests on counting alone and is bounded only by our search effort.
res.caveats: All numbers are for one random base message (Rng(msgseed=7) words) except the zero-base runs; the reduced-round biases are byte-lane phenomena and their exact magnitudes (e.g. the 2^-3.7 at R=3, the exact 3/8 for bit 0 under c3 at R=1) depend on the base word values, which I did not vary beyond zero vs. random; the qualitative picture (which byte positions leak, and the U-count at which the signal disappears) is expected to be base-independent but that is a conjecture, not measured. The mechanism sketch (a -1 or 2^40 difference stays inside one byte lane of the ZipperMerge and is blocked from lane 0 until a Permute moves it) is a reading of the code, confirmed only indirectly by the state-difference snapshots (737/1024 constant difference bits at r=0 for c3); I did not derive the R=1 constants analytically. No chi-square 'z' above 37.05 is meaningful (p-value floor 1e-300). The per-bit test is blind to collision rates below ~2^-12 at 2^28 keys; the only collision bounds here are the direct counts (0 in 2^31 for w3+2^40, 0 in 2^30.3 for w3-1 at R=3/R=4, 0 in 2^28 for every other pair at R=4). Multiple comparisons: about 10^4 statistics were examined in total, so isolated |z| in 4-4.6 (e.g. bit63 R=2 z=6.54 was above that, w1-2^24 R=3 z=4.09 in the scan was not replicated) should be read with that in mind; every claim above rests on |z| >= 5.6 or on independent replication. The scan used only 2^24 keys per cell (threshold 2^-11.5), so weaker R=3/R=4 cells could exist; sign of the difference (+/-) made no difference in any cell. bias2's first output file and both wybias files carry a stale 'rounds' label in the JSON header (arrays are correct; analyze.py corrects it; documented in README). Machine was shared (load 170-340); wall times in timing.log are for scheduling only and support no throughput claim. Nothing in the repository was modified; all files are under the scratchpad directory listed above.

verdicts.claim: The full 4-round HighwayHash-64 shows no detectable difference bias: across 54 (pair,length,D) configurations at 2^28 random keys (word complements, +2^32, single-bit flips, +-1, +-2^40, random pair; 32 and 64 bytes) no statistic (64 per-bit z's, byte chi-squares, Hamming-weight tests) exceeded |z| = 3.83, and for the strongest reduced-round pair (w3 += 2^40, 32 B) a pooled 2^31-key sample gives max per-bit |z| 2.59, byte chi-square max |z| 2.12 and 0 collisions (rate < 2^-29.4 at 95%), i.e. per-bit bias < 2^-14.5.

v.reasoning:
The measured numbers reproduce, but several parts of the claim are stated more precisely or more strongly than the evidence supports.

CONFIRMED (independent recomputation, experiment/angles/verify-difference-bias/recheck.py and checkdiffs.py, README.md has the commands):
- Their modified highwayhash.c differs from tools/bench/adversarial/vendor/highwayhash/c/highwayhash.c only by 43 appended lines (HighwayHash64Rounds/Multi/Multi4); HighwayHash64 is untouched. I rebuilt validate.c: all 65 kExpected64 vectors + the kTestKey2 vector pass, and Multi4[3] == HighwayHash64 on those and 20000 random inputs, so the R=4 column is the real hash (no off-by-one in round counting).
- The m0/m1 hex in every JSON matches its label (w0 +2^32, bit 0/63 of w0, word complements, wK -= 1, w3/w7 += 2^40, independent random m1); little-endian words = packet lanes as in the C source.
- Max over all 4650 R=4 statistics in the 31 JSONs (64 per-bit z for xor and sub, all 8 byte chi-squares, HW chi-square/mean/variance) is 3.83 (L64 c01, D_xor bit 3); largest byte chi-square |z| is 2.96; 0 collisions in every R=4 sample. A max of 3.83 over ~4650 (correlated) statistics is exactly what the null predicts (P(max<=3.83) ~ 0.55).
- Pooled p3s40 32 B (seeds 21+31, N=2^31): max per-bit |z| = 2.59 (xor, bit 15, bias -2.79e-5 = 2^-15.1), byte chi-square max |z| 2.12, 0 collisions; 3/2^31 = 2^-29.4 is the correct rule-of-three 95% bound.

OVERSTATED / WRONG:
1. "54 (pair,length,D) configurations at 2^28": there are 28 files / 56 rows at 2^28 (62 rows in all). Two of those rows are a byte-identical duplicate: L32_c3_zero_n28.json and B2_L32_s1w3_zero_n28.json are the same pair (~0 = 0-1) run with the same seed 1 (identical R=4 counters, md5 6794fa2d...). L32_c3 seed 1 and seed 2 are the same pair with fresh keys. D=xor and D=sub are two statistics on one sample, not two configurations. Distinct (length, m0, m1) pairs at 2^28: 26 (15 at 32 B, 11 at 64 B); 27 with p3s40 (2^30 only). All seed-1 runs also share one key set.
2. "+-1" and "+-2^40": at 2^28 only wK -= 1 (w0..w3 at 32 B, w3/w7 at 64 B) and wK += 2^40 (w3 at 32/64 B, w7 at 64 B) were run with the full statistic set. wK += 1 and wK -= 2^40 appear only in the 2^24-key scan (per-bit max |z| and collision count only, per-bit threshold ~2^-11.5). "single-bit flips" is bits 0 and 63 of w0 at 32 B only.
3. "per-bit bias < 2^-14.5" is not a bound: 2^-14.5 = 2/sqrt(2^31) is the |z|=4 detection threshold. The observed worst-bit estimate is 2^-15.1; the one-sided 95% upper bound for that bit is (2.59+1.645)/(2 sqrt 2^31) = 2^-14.4, and a simultaneous (Bonferroni over 128 bit tests) 95% bound is (2.59+3.36)/(2 sqrt 2^31) = 2^-13.9.
4. The HOW TO CHECK command does not print 3.83: awk '{print $12}' selects the z_HWmean column in the SUMMARY rows and a "z=..." string in the per-file lines; it prints "z=+2.41". Column 13 (max|z|_all) gives 3.83 (and that column omits the max-over-8-bytes chi-square, which I checked separately: max 2.96).
5. analyze.py's z_var divides by sqrt(480/N); for Bin(64,1/2) mu4 = 16(1+3*62/4) = 760, so Var((X-mu)^2) = 504. z_var is inflated by 2.5% (max 3.00 -> 2.93). No conclusion changes.

res.lens: lane-locality: lane structure of HighwayHash's 64-bit output (lane 0 only) and how many finalization rounds a single-lane difference needs to reach it
res.summary: Structural fact (code reading, confirmed empirically): HighwayHash's Update mixes lanes only within the pairs {0,1} and {2,3} (per-lane multiplies, then ZipperMerge within 128-bit halves); the two 512-bit halves of the 1024-bit state interact ONLY through the Permute (lanes 2,3,0,1) of the finalization, and the 64-bit output is v0[0]+v1[0]+mul0[0]+mul1[0]. After a 2- or 3-packet message with the difference in lane 3 of packet 0, all eight {0,1}-half words were unchanged for 100% of 2^24 keys, so the crossing must happen inside the R=4 finalization rounds. ZipperMerge routes a lane's own bytes {0,1,2,3,5} back to itself and only bytes {4,6,7} to its partner, and the lane multiplies (lo32*hi32) put their XOR difference almost entirely in the low 33 bits (mul0 byte-change map one Update after a -1 difference: bytes 0-3 0.996, byte 4 0.50, byte 5 0.002, bytes 6-7 ~0), so narrow differences cross slowly. Analytic no-carry byte-set model (reach.py) first-round-reachable table for a -1 difference (complement of a zero word, = bit-0 flip): lane 0 -> lane-0 words v0/v1/mul0 at r=0, mul1[0] at r=1; lane 1 -> v1[0] at r=0, v0[0],mul1[0] at r=1, mul0[0] at r=2; lane 2 -> v0[0],v1[0],mul0[0] at r=1, mul1[0] at r=2; lane 3 -> nothing in lane 0 before r=2; wide (complement of a random word): all lane-0 words by r=0 (lane 0) or r=1 (lanes 1-3); bit-63 flip: all four lane-0 words only at r=2 for every lane. Empirically (unmodified reference C with the finalization stopped after r rounds; 2^26 random 4-word keys): -1 difference in lane 3 of a 32-byte message leaves all four lane-0 words unchanged for 99.6% of keys after r=1 (64-bit collision rate 66842413/2^26 = 0.996), still collides at r=2 with rate 80/2^26 = 2^-19.7 (mul0[0] unchanged for 99.6% and mul1[0] for 36.5% of keys at r=2), and 0/2^26 at r=3 and r=4; the same differential on the paper's pseudo-random base (bit-0 flip, 2^22 keys) gives 0.996, 4/2^22, 0, 0. Bit-63 flip in lane 2: collision rate 0.4998 (8385180/2^24) at r=1 (a bit-31 packet difference carries into the high half of v1[1] for half the keys), 0 from r=2 on. Per-bit avalanche of the 64-bit output (2^22 keys, criterion every bit within 0.005 of 1/2): first clean round is 3 for the narrow differentials in the far half (-1 in lanes 2,3; bit-63 in lanes 1,3), 2 for -1 in lanes 0,1 and bit-63 in lanes 0,2, and 1-2 for the wide complement; at r=2 the worst case (-1, lane 3) has 38 of 64 bits flipping with p<0.45 (mean 0.317). At r=3 and r=4 all 64 bits of all 20 runs are within 0.001 of 1/2. So the smallest R that fully diffuses every lane into the 64-bit output is 3, and HighwayHash64's 4 rounds leave one spare round (two for a wide difference); for the 128-bit output the first clean round is 3 (2 for wide), leaving three of six spare. Extra message packets act as within-half rounds (-1 in lane 3 + 1 filler packet: 32/2^24 = 2^-19.0 collisions at r=1, clean at r=2; + 2 filler packets: clean at r=1). At the real R=4, no single-word differential collided in 2^26 keys (2^24 for bit-63, 2^22 for paper/lsb), and all 1048575 additive output differences over 2^20 keys were distinct for every configuration.

res.paper_relevance: Gives the paper a structural, non-search argument about HighwayHash for the appendix's per-hash paragraph: its state is two independent 512-bit halves during absorption, the 64-bit output is one lane, and the only cross-half mixing is the four-round finalization, of which one round is spare on the diffusion criterion (a two-round variant would score about 21 bits on the paper's scale: log2(4 words / 2^-19.7) = 21.7 at 32 B, versus the shipped four rounds where nothing was found). It supports listing HighwayHash with a '>=' entry based on search effort (0/2^26 for the lane-local differentials) while explaining WHY differential search finds nothing at four rounds and what the design margin is, which is the kind of 'other way to think about it' the author asked for. It also supplies a concrete comparison point with the multiply-fold hashes: the same low-half concentration of the multiply difference exists in HighwayHash's lane multiplies, but it is repaired by three subsequent rounds rather than exposed by a single fold.
res.suggested_text: HighwayHash's Update mixes lanes only within the pairs \{0,1\} and \{2,3\}: during absorption the 1024-bit state is two independent 512-bit halves, which interact solely through the Permute step of the finalization, and the 64-bit output is read from lane 0 alone. A difference placed in lane 3 of the last packet therefore has to cross halves during the four finalization rounds. Stopping the finalization early (a probe built on the unmodified reference C, checked against its published test vectors) shows how much margin that crossing has: with a single-word complement of a zero word in lane 3 of a 32-byte message, one round leaves all four lane-0 state words unchanged for 99.6\% of keys, two rounds still give a collision rate of $2^{-19.7}$ ($80/2^{26}$), and three rounds are the first at which every output bit flips with probability $1/2 \pm 0.001$ over $2^{22}$ keys. The shipped four rounds thus leave one spare round on this criterion (two for a complement of a random word; three of six for the 128-bit output). At four rounds we observed no collision in $2^{26}$ keys for any single-word differential and no repeated additive output difference among $2^{20}$ keys, so the table entry is a search bound, not a proof.
res.caveats: Coverage: only single-word differentials (complement of a zero word = -1, complement of the paper's random base word, bit-63 flip, bit-0 flip) in one lane of a 32-byte message, plus three 64/96-byte variants with the difference in packet 0; no multi-word or cancelling differentials, no UpdateRemainder lengths (not multiples of 32), no key-dependent or chosen-message-content searches beyond the two base messages. The 'fully diffused' criterion is a strict-avalanche heuristic (per-bit flip probability within 0.005, resp. 0.001, of 1/2 at 2^22 keys, standard error 0.00024 per bit) and not a collision bound; clean avalanche at r=3 does not prove the r=3 collision rate is 2^-64, only that none of 2^26 keys collided. Zero collisions in 2^26 keys at r=4 bounds those pairs' collision rate at roughly < 2^-25 with 95% confidence and says nothing about other pairs. The analytic model (reach.py) ignores carries/borrows and product cancellations; it reproduces the dominant paths but misses probability-1/2 carry events when a difference sits at bit 31 of a packet word (msb/lane 2, r=1) and the ~2^-8 borrow events visible in the byte maps. The 'unchanged' fractions at r=1,2 (0.996, 0.417, 0.365, 0.168 etc.) are measured, their mechanistic explanations in the README are my reading of the code, verified only through the byte maps. Machine was shared (load ~200); runs used 3 threads; no timing statements are made. All runs use the exact seeds recorded in run_all.sh/run_extra.sh; the additive-difference statistic covers 1048575 (not 2^20) samples per run because the budget is split over 3 threads. No repository file was modified; the probe includes the unmodified vendored highwayhash.c.

res.lens: weak-keys-init: weak-key classes and the public initial multipliers of HighwayHash, analytically
res.summary: The key enters only v0 = init0^key and v1 = init1^rot32(key); mul0, mul1 start as the public constants, so at packet 1 the lane-i mul0 product lo32(v1[i])*hi32(v0[i]) depends only on hi32(key[i]) and the mul1 product only on lo32(key[i]) (plus one carry bit). The mul0 update is dead in lane i exactly when hi32(key[i]) = hi32(init0[i]) (2^-32 per lane, message-independent; density of some dead lane = 1-(1-2^-32)^4 = (2^98-6*2^64+2^34-1)/2^128 = 2^-30.0000000005). Tracing single-lane differences through the byte permutation of ZipperMerge (table verified by simulation) shows every multiply that sees a difference costs a 32-bit event, that no packet-1 pair can equalise v0 or (v0,v1) (probability 0, the update is a permutation), and that a full state collision needs at least three packets. The best geometry is lane 0, byte 1: a +2^8 difference in packet 1 maps to v0[0] byte 5 then v1[0] byte 3, and at packet 2 the cancelling -2^8 difference and the v0 byte-5 difference feed the SAME multiply lo32(v1[0])*hi32(v0[0]), whose products coincide iff lo32(v1[0]) - hi32(v0[0]) = 2^8. Under condition 1 the two operands are add/xor/byte-shuffle functions of the key with no multiplication in them, so their difference D0 is uniform in its low 24 bits but its top byte takes only four values (0x4c..0x4f; 0x4d for 85.6% of keys with low24(D0) < 2^12 over 2^31 samples), and the attacker aligns it with the packet-2 constant c2lo = 0xb3000100. Measured with condition 1 forced and the rest of the key uniform: 208/2^32, 95/2^31 and 16/2^28 collisions (pooled 319/6710886400 = 2^-24.33), every hit a full 1024-bit state collision colliding in HighwayHash64, 128 and 256 simultaneously, and 0 collisions outside condition 2 when every key was hashed (2^28). Total collision probability of the fixed 96-byte pair over uniformly random 256-bit keys: 2^-32 (exact) x 2^-24.33 (measured) = 2^-56.3, about 2^7.7 times the generic 2^-64 for the 64-bit output and 2^72 / 2^200 times the ideal for the 128-/256-bit outputs; it survives any common suffix (128 B extension checked). Controls over 2^28 uniformly random keys: 0 collisions at 32, 64 and 96 B (expected 2^-28). Step-1 word statistics over 2^28 random keys match the predicted difference pattern exactly (v0[0] +2^40, v1[0] +2^8+2^24, mul0[0] differs, v1[1] differs at 2^-8.0, v0[1] and mul1[0] at 2^-24.2, everything else equal in every trial). An explicit colliding key with its two messages is recorded and re-verified against the reference linked as a separate translation unit.
